title: US Department of Energy Releases National Quantum Roadmap Establishing 2028 Fault-Tolerance Milestones - Quantum Computing Report
gist: The DOE Office of Science Advisory Committee's Quantum Subcommittee, chaired by Anna Grassellino, published a three-phase national quantum roadmap targeting a scientifically relevant error-corrected quantum capability by 2028. It shifts federal evaluation from physical qubit counts to demonstrated scientific utility and stays modality-neutral.

insights.claim: The US DOE Office of Science Advisory Committee Quantum Subcommittee, chaired by Anna Grassellino of Fermilab with Supratik Guha as vice-chair, published a national strategy targeting a scientifically relevant, error-corrected quantum computing capability by 2028.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: A dated federal fault-tolerance milestone gives quantum vendors and investors a concrete 2028 benchmark to track.

insights.claim: The roadmap is aligned with the Administration's Quantum Genesis Initiative and the DOE Q Competition, tying the report to existing federal quantum programs.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Suggests the strategy is likely to be backed by funding vehicles already in motion.
insights.locator: Aligned with the Administration's Quantum Genesis Initiative

insights.claim: The SCAC report mandates that federal quantum investments be judged by demonstrated scientific utility rather than raw physical qubit counts.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Vendors marketing on qubit count may lose federal favor; favor those showing error-corrected, application-relevant results.
insights.quote: replacing physical qubit counts with demonstrated scientific utility
insights.locator: The SCAC report mandates a fundamental metric shift

insights.claim: Progress will be measured by a system's ability to run intractable calculations in quantum chemistry, drug discovery, catalytic material design, fusion plasma simulation and high-energy physics.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Defines the target application domains for federal quantum demand: chemistry, materials, pharma and fusion.
insights.locator: Rather than evaluating hardware solely through raw physical qubit numbers

insights.claim: Phase I (2026-2028) runs Quantum Grand Challenges: competitive multidisciplinary challenges with national lab, university and industry co-design of hardware, algorithms and software to show error-corrected scientific utility by 2028.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Competitive challenges imply near-term award opportunities for vendors that partner with labs.

insights.claim: Phase II creates a DOE Quantum Computing User Facility with on-premises, co-located QPU hardware that replaces opaque black-box cloud APIs with open, co-developed control stacks, cryogenics and hardware architectures.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Favors vendors willing to deploy on-premises and open their stacks over cloud-only access providers.
insights.quote: Replaces opaque “black-box” cloud APIs with open, co-developed control stacks, cryogenics, and hardware architectures
insights.locator: Phase II: DOE Quantum Computing User Facility (QCUF)

insights.claim: Phase III (2030+) embeds quantum co-processors, simulators and sensors into leadership supercomputers such as Frontier and Aurora, forming a hybrid quantum-HPC-AI network.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Quantum is positioned as an HPC accelerator, so integration with classical and AI stacks becomes a key differentiator.

insights.claim: The roadmap aims to move QPUs from isolated lab instruments to integrated co-processors across DOE's HPC and AI infrastructure.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Hybrid quantum-classical software and interconnect layers are the likely enabling market.
insights.locator: Aligned with the Administration's Quantum Genesis Initiative

insights.claim: The SCAC report takes a modality-neutral stance, advocating continued co-design investment across superconducting circuits, neutral atoms, trapped ions, photonics and silicon spin qubits.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: No federal winner-picking among modalities; diversified exposure across hardware approaches is consistent with policy.

insights.claim: To speed technology transfer, the report recommends 6-to-18-month embedded co-design fellowships, joint laboratory-industry personnel appointments and open interconnect standards for hybrid classical-quantum software stacks.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Open interconnect standards could favor interoperable software vendors and reduce lock-in.
insights.locator: Furthermore, the report recommends new partnership models
